The map data for the year 800 names this area "Rajput Clans and Small States". It covers the middle of mainland Southeast Asia, from eastern Burma across Thailand and Laos. The name looks like a slip in the map data: the Rajput clans ruled in northern India, far to the west, not here. The map here prints "Small states" instead.

In 800 this area held many small states and chiefdoms rather than one great power:

  • Mon kingdoms of the Dvaravati culture in the Chao Phraya valley, Buddhist and trading with India;
  • the Pyu city-states of central Burma to the west;
  • Khmer princedoms of Chenla in the east, just before the rise of the Khmer Empire in 802;
  • hill peoples in the north, on the edge of the kingdom of Nanzhao in Yunnan.

Tai-speaking peoples had not yet moved south in large numbers. They came over the following centuries and later founded the kingdoms of Sukhothai and Ayutthaya.
